newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: U.S. investors target Bangladesh's energy sector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investors target Bangladesh's energy sector.

text.p: American investment is not likely to come easily into Bangladesh, but the U.S. investor's eye is on the country's potential gas and power sector, U.S. officials said on Tuesday.

"I don't think we can expect U.S. investment in sectors other than natural resources," Forrest Cookson, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh, told a news conference ahead of a U.S. trade show.
Some 160 American firms will be represented at the sixth trade show on Thursday.
He said American investment in Bangladesh was insignificant. "There has not been an increase in American investment in Bangladesh," he said.
Cookson said the American apathy was mainly because of the small size of the Bangladesh market. "The domestic market has not grown enough to attract American investors," he said.
Tim Fosyth, economic and commercial officer at the U.S. embassy in Dhaka, said American investments were expected in Bangladesh's power sector.

"There is good possibility of U.S. investment in power plants when the level may double or treble. The U.S. firms are also interested in telecom sector. We expect U.S. companies will be winning some bids," he said.

He said U.S. investment in Bangladesh was negligible at the moment but it could run up $200 million after Halliburton and Occidental International and Exploration Company signed contracts for gas exploration.
Fosyth said foreign investors would like to see the present political stability extended for their presence in Bangladesh.

Political stability has been restored since Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina took power in a peaceful election in last June. The investment climate has also improved after the new government vowed to pursue a free market economy and liberalised trade and investment.

Cookson said trade between the two countries had gradually developed. The balance of trade is over $1.0 billion in favour of Bangladesh, thanks largely to Bangladesh garment exports to the United States.

Bangladesh's exports to the United States in the first six months of 1996 reached $590 million against imports of $101 million. In 1995 the country's exports were $1.257 billion against imports of $325 million.
